data.title: Moody's Upgrades Hungary Outlook, Citing Improved EU Relations
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Moody's Ratings changed its outlook on Hungary's government to stable from negative.

Alongside that, it affirmed Hungary's Baa2 long-term issuer and senior unsecured ratings and its Baa2 foreign-currency senior unsecured shelf rating.

Moody's said the upgraded outlook reflects reforms and improvement in Hungary's relations with the European Union. That improved relationship has reduced governance-related risks.

Anti-corruption institutions in the country have also strengthened. Renewed access to E.U. resources, improved investor sentiment and a concrete fiscal consolidation program all support prospects of economic growth and lower debt.

The Baa2 ratings reflect a balance between Hungary's relatively high income levels and diversified economy with its elevated government debt and continuing policy constraints.

Moody's also upgraded the issuer rating of Hungary's national bank to stable from negative, affirming the Baa2 issuer rating. The bank's credit profile is closely intertwined with the government and is influenced by the same credit fundamentals, Moody's said.

Hungary's local and foreign currency ceilings remain unchanged at A1.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: Iovance Biotherapeutics Reports Inducement Grants under NASDAQ Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
data.description:
PHILADELPHIA, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc. ("Iovance" or the “Company”), a commercial biotechnology company focused on innovating, developing, and delivering novel polyclonal tumor infiltrating lymphocyte (“TIL”) therapies for patients with cancer, today announced that on November 19, 2026 (the “Date of Grant”), the Company approved the grant of inducement stock options covering an aggregate of 175,840 shares of Iovance’s common stock to twenty-two new, non-executive employees.

The awards were granted under Iovance’s Amended and Restated 2021 Inducement Plan, which provides for the granting of equity awards to new employees of Iovance by the Company’s compensation committee in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). Each of the stock options granted as referenced in this press release has an exercise price of $7.31, the closing price of Iovance’s common stock on the Date of Grant. Each stock option vests over a three-year period, with one-third of the shares vesting on the first anniversary of the employee’s start date (the “First Vesting Date”) and the remaining shares vesting in eight quarterly installments over the next two years, commencing with the first quarter following the First Vesting Date, subject to continued employment with the Company through the applicable vesting dates.

About Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc.

Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc. is the global leader in innovating, developing, and delivering tumor infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) cell therapies for patients with solid tumors. Amtagvi® (lifileucel) is the first FDA-approved, one-time treatment for previously treated advanced melanoma, now approved in three global markets and available at more than 100 authorized treatment centers (ATCs). The Iovance TIL platform spans registrational trials and next-generation programs in additional solid tumors, including gene-edited and IL-12 tethered TIL therapies, next-generation IL-2, and precision immuno-oncology approaches. As the first and only company to take TIL therapy from concept to a broadly accessible commercial treatment, Iovance operates as an end-to-end cell therapy company, anchored by fully owned, centralized U.S.-based manufacturing that is scaled to serve thousands of cancer patients worldwide each year. Headquartered in Pennsylvania with offices and laboratories in California and Florida, Iovance serves patients at ATCs and clinical sites across almost the entire U.S. and in many countries around the world. For more information, please visit www.iovance.com.

Amtagvi® and its accompanying design marks, Proleukin®, Iovance®, and IovanceCares™ are trademarks and registered trademarks of Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc. or its subsidiaries. All other trademarks and registered trademarks are the property of their respective owners.

Information on Iovance’s broad, industry-leading patent portfolio is available on the Intellectual Property page on www.iovance.com.

data.title: Charlie’s Holdings (OTCQB: CHUC) Reports Growth of 19% to $11.3 Million Revenue for First Nine Months 2026
data.description:
Received highly favorable notification from the FDA on 56 PMTA SKUs for inclusion on a list of products against which FDA does not intend to prioritize enforcement

PACHA age-gated products will be America's first age-gated disposables

COSTA MESA, CA, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Charlie’s Holdings, Inc. (OTCQB: CHUC) (“Charlie’s” or the “Company”), an industry leader in the premium vapor products space, reported results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and provided an update on recent business highlights.

Key Financial Highlights for First Nine Months 2026 (compared to first nine months 2025)

  • Revenue increased 19% to $11.3 million
  • Gross profit decreased 3% to $2.4 million
  • Operating loss increased 75% to $3.9 million

Key Balance Sheet Highlights as of September 30, 2026 (compared to December 2025)

  • Cash balance of $0.4 million, compared to $1.3 million
  • Total assets of $11.2 million, compared to $11.6 million
  • Total stockholders’ equity of $1.4 million, compared to $3.4 million

Management Commentary

“Because billions of dollars of illicit vapor products – made by Chinese manufacturers who thumb their noses at the FDA – have flooded the United States this year, Charlie’s sales and profits have taken a hit,” reported Henry Sicignano, President and CEO. “Fortunately, we have the inventory, and the opportunity, to reestablish growing, profitable sales in several states where regulatory enforcement has again become a priority. In this environment, we have redoubled our commitment to regulatory compliance as well as our initiatives to monetize the Company’s 678-SKU PMTA portfolio.”

Mr. Sicignano continued, “Big Tobacco ‘pod systems’ are outdated, provide very low puff counts, and offer few flavor choices. Charlie’s products are modern disposable products… offering much higher puff counts… and hundreds of flavors that adult consumers strongly prefer. For all these reasons, we believe Charlie’s PACHA product line is the best, most robust portfolio of PMTA products in the industry and will likely represent significant value to one or more Big Tobacco strategic partners in 2027.”

As previously reported, Charlie’s has made the well-considered decision to focus intensely on the two strategic priorities that matter most to Company shareholders:

1) Management has shifted its priorities from sales of the PACHAMAMA and SBX product lines to a laser focus on the beta test pilot of PACHA age-gated disposables. The Company has already received tens of thousands of finished age-gated PACHA products in its warehouse. Management has secured test-market purchase commitments from retailers. As soon as the Company’s software licensor completes final tests of its “second generation” consumer app, Charlie’s will begin shipping the age-gated PACHA product to stores. The Company expects that Charlie’s PACHA age-gated products will be America’s first age-gated disposables.

2) The Company has redeployed the priorities of one of Charlie’s largest shareholders. Ryan Stump, Charlie’s co-founder and former COO, has begun work to identify and pursue strategic transactions and/or partnerships with leading global tobacco companies to significantly enhance long-term value for Charlie’s shareholders.

Regulatory Developments

FDA Enforcement Priorities Guidance

In August 2026, the FDA notified Charlie’s that certain of its PACHA products (56 SKUs) for which PMTAs have been submitted have been tentatively identified for inclusion on the FDA's public-facing webpage of products for which the FDA generally does not intend to prioritize enforcement of premarket authorization requirements — a development the Company views as highly favorable. Inclusion on the FDA’s new list of “low-enforcement priority products” does not, however, constitute FDA marketing authorization, preclude case-by-case enforcement, or bear on whether any PMTA will ultimately be granted. Accordingly, Charlie’s intends to continue pursuing FDA review of its pending PMTAs and to comply with all applicable requirements.

FDA has validated age-gating as a pathway for the legal sale of flavored Electronic Nicotine Delivery System (“ENDS”) products

In May 2026, the FDA granted marketing orders for four Glas Inc. pod products, including “Gold” (mango) and “Sapphire” (blueberry) flavored, age-gated pods. This landmark development validates “age-gating” as a legitimate pathway for the legal sale of flavored ENDS products in the United States. However, Juul Labs filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Glas, Inc. and, under these circumstances, Glas’ newly authorized “fruit flavored” products are unlikely to go on the market in the near term; it is likely that Charlie’s PACHA age-gated products will be America’s first age-gated disposables.

Business Catalysts

Charlie’s plans to begin beta testing PACHA age-gated flavored disposables.

In December 2025, the Company signed a definitive licensing agreement to commercialize the first-ever AI-powered blockchain-based age-gating system for vapor products in the United States. Scheduled to beta test this year, the PACHA test-market initiative will incorporate the age-gating system in a special line of the Company’s flavored ENDS disposables; simultaneously, Charlie’s intends to amend certain of its existing PMTAs with the FDA for PACHA brand ENDS with the youth access prevention system.

Mr. Sicignano commented, “Charlie’s plans to launch PACHA products that have not yet received final FDA authorization follows the example set by one of America’s largest tobacco companies… In recent months, RJ Reynolds' Vuse business began selling four new fruit flavor pods (berry, fresh mint, peach, and watermelon), all of which were issued FDA Marketing Denial Orders (MDOs). Given that Reynolds has demonstrated it is willing to pursue flavored ENDS commercialization strategies, before final FDA authorization, we believe the strategic calculus for Charlie’s – and for our potential strategic partners – has improved. Dramatically.”

Charlie’s will monetize the Company’s PMTAs through new strategic partnerships

In 2025, in three separate transactions, Charlie's sold sixteen of the Company's PACHA synthetic nicotine PMTA products and related assets for $7.5 million in cash plus a contingent one-time payment of up to $4.2 million. In the last of the three transactions, the buyer purchased a single Charlie’s PMTA product for $1 million. Based on these sales, taking into account the fact that Charlie’s continues to own 678 PMTA products, and considering the interest other companies have expressed in Charlie's portfolio, the Company believes Charlie's remaining PMTA products, as a stand-alone asset, could have a monetary value that significantly exceeds the Company’s current market cap.

Financial Results for the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026:

data.title: U.S. Dollar Ends Roughly Flat Amid Rising Expectations On Fed Tightening
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The U.S. Dollar value ended almost flat on Friday after several U.S. Federal Reserve officials concurred on the need to raise the interest rates in the December meeting while the U.S.-Iran stalemate continues with no resolution in sight.

Today, the U.S. Dollar Index DXY, which measures the Greenback against a basket of other major currencies, was last seen trading at 103.88, down by 0.01 (or 0.01%).

While against the Euro, the USD was trading at 1.096, up by 0.03%, against the GBP, the USD was trading at 1.308, up by 0.05%.

Against the USD, the Japanese Yen was trading at 158.584, up by 0.69%, the Swiss Franc was trading at 0.840, up by 0.41%; and the Canadian Dollar was trading at 1.435, down by 0.09%.

Against one unit of Australian Dollar, the USD was trading at 0.662, up by 0.61%.

In the U.S., the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index was revised higher to 51.5 in November 2026, from a preliminary estimate of 51.0, marking its highest level in three months.

Yesterday, in a speech before the Money Marketeers of New York University, the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson remarked that inflation needs to be the policy priority currently as the labor market is at full employment.

Anna Paulson stressed that the way to bring down inflation is by raising interest rates though she advocated adopting a step-by-step increase rather than a drastic move to allow time for the economy to adjust to higher costs.

Earlier, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee stated that he would consider all options available to counter stubborn U.S. inflation.

Over the past few days, several other senior Fed officials have expressed support for a rate hike.

The Federal Open Market Committee is slated to hold its next meeting on December 8-9.

On Wednesday, the minutes of the FOMC's October meeting was released. Notably, the report stated that almost all participants were in agreement that rate raise would be appropriate to bring inflation to the 2.00% objective.

The committee had voted 10-2 last month to hold the benchmark federal funds rate in the 3.75% to 4.00% range while Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented and wanted a quarter-percentage point hike.

Hours before the release of the Minutes of Meeting, Fed Governor Christopher Waller stated that the Fed needs to 'shock people' with a half-percentage-point increase in the coming meeting.

With regard to the U.S.-Iran crisis, speaking separately to Reuters, Fox News, and Axios, U.S. President Donald Trump clearly stated that he is not rushing to any decision on Iran and wanted to see what happens after January 1, 2027.

While economists are unable to comprehend the logic behind Trump's decision and the significance of the date, for now, markets are relieved of war anxiety. However, experts are concerned that Trump could possibly reverse his decision in the intervening time.

Meanwhile, according to a report by Financial Times, senior officials in the U.S. and Israel are urging Trump to restart strikes on Iran, as the American military planners warn that their forces risk becoming overextended if the stalemate continues into the new year.

Reportedly, the U.S. Central Command has briefed American officials that the toll on forces from a sustained military build-up past the end of December could erode military readiness.

According to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, currently investors are betting on a 91.50% chance of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike at the upcoming meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve on December 8-9 while the odds on the rates being held at the current level stand at 8.50%.

Due to increasing rate hike concerns, gold prices went into a tailspin today, falling nearly more than 4.00%.

data.title: Sonoro Energy Announces Adoption Of Semi-Annual Financial Reporting Framework
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

CALGARY, ALBERTA – November 20, 2026 – TheNewswire - Sonoro Energy Ltd. ("Sonoro" or the "Company") announces its intention to adopt the semi-annual financial reporting pilot program ("SAR Pilot Program") and rely on the exemptions provided under Coordinated Blanket Order 51-933 – Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers (the "Blanket Order").

The SAR Pilot Program, implemented under the Blanket Order, permits eligible venture issuers listed on the TSX Venture Exchange or the Canadian Securities Exchange to voluntarily transition from quarterly to semi-annual financial reporting, subject to the terms and conditions of the Blanket Order.

By adopting the SAR Pilot Program, Sonoro expects to reduce the administrative burden and costs associated with quarterly financial reporting, allowing the Company to direct additional resources toward its business development activities and the advancement of its oil and gas opportunities in Canada and internationally.

In reliance of the Blanket Order, Sonoro will not file interim financial statements and related management discussion and analysis for the three and nine month period ending September 30, 2026 and three month period ended March 31, 2027 and similar periods moving forward. Sonoro confirms that it meets the SAR Pilot’s eligibility criteria which includes being a venture issuer with annual revenues of less than $10 million and maintaining a clean 12-month continuous disclosure record.

The Company will continue to file its audited annual financial statements and related MD&A within 120 days of its financial year-end, together with its six-month interim financial statements and related MD&A within 60 days of the end of the second quarter.

Sonoro remains committed to timely disclosure and will continue to comply with all applicable continuous disclosure obligations, including the requirement to promptly disclose material changes and significant developments affecting the Company.

data.title: U.S. Stocks Extend Plunge as AI Boom Turns to Bust — Update
data.description:
By Rob Curran

U.S. stocks plunged and an index of mega-cap technology stocks skirted bear-market territory as predictions of a speculative bust in artificial-intelligence stocks appeared to come to fruition.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 949.73 points, or 1.93%, to 48147.33 and entered into correction territory having fallen more than 10% from its record high in August. The S&P 500 dropped 265.44 points, or 3.70%, to 6910.39, also entered into a correction following its October peak. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite sank 1261.47 points, or 5.28%, to 22617.73, and came close to bear-market territory, a decline of 20% or more from its peak, during the session.

The Nasdaq 100, a basket of the largest tech companies that is tracked by many tech-oriented investment and retirement funds, closed at 25028.98, an almost 20% fall from its record high last month.

Anthropic's shares tumbled 9.1% to $88.30 as fear of missing out on the Claude chatbot maker's IPO gave way to skepticism about its profit outlook. One strategist said market emphasis shifted this week from Anthropic's voracious demand for chips to its ability to translate that computing power to profits.

"They were telling us the narrative: 'We are going to print money with this compute,'" said Joe Tigay, portfolio manager at money-management firm Equity Armor Investments. "We need this compute to figure it out, and eventually we'll grow into it, and AI is going to be something everybody needs, it's going to be the greatest thing in the world.'"

Now that Anthropic is public, Tigay said, the message from investors is: "'Show me, show me how this is going to turn into profit for you guys and eventually for the whole economy, thus lifting market higher.'"

Anthropic came within 5 cents of its $83 IPO price at session lows, and was down 28% from its Thursday peak.

Tigay said it was possible that the rout continued, mushrooming into something like the Dotcom bust or the 19th century railroad panic. But that still would not mean that AI would be remembered as a net negative for the U.S. economy, he said.

"Look at Amazon...they went public in the middle of that run and struggled for many years before really taking off and becoming a really profitable company," Tigay said. "It's possible Anthropic can go through that, and we'll look back and say they weren't making money yet but they had great leadership, a great product and they were just chugging away at it."

Nvidia shares slid 14% to $125.53 as the maker of the graphics processing units that are the cornerstone of AI data centers lost 23% for the week. That was the company's biggest weekly loss since the financial crisis of October 2008. It was former Chief Executive Jensen Huang's abrupt downfall last week that sparked the flight from AI companies last week.

Arkansas Sen. Tom Cotton, Republican, said Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick repeatedly ignored warnings that U.S. AI chips were being smuggled to China before the recent problems at Nvidia became public.

CoreWeave shares slid 12% to $39.51, slipping below the company's 2025 IPO price. Originally founded as a cryptocurrency mining firm, CoreWeave pivoted to use its data-center and cloud expertise to provide AI computing power, partnering with Nvidia as an exclusive chip supplier. The two companies fortunes are linked as Nvidia's holds an equity stake in its customer CoreWeave.

President Trump said he would block U.S. tech companies from building data centers overseas, at a White House press conference.

A significant portion of Nvidia's chip business is in Asia, and a stoppage of sales to that region could cause data-center demand and chip prices to slump, Equity Armor Investments' Tigay said

Shares of SpaceX, the other big AI-related company to go public this year, posted a loss of 7.7% to $127.79, falling below its IPO price of $135.

The U.S. dollar ticked down, but finished the week just off its 2026 highs.

Dollar-sensitive gold futures slid 4.6% to $3512.30 a troy ounce, and lost 9.5% for the week, the most since March. Silver futures plummeted 16% for the week, closing at $41.035 a troy ounce.

Safe-haven demand caused a sharp decline in Treasury yields.

The yield on the policy-sensitive two-year Treasury lost 0.166 percentage point to 4.611%, completing its biggest weekly loss in more than two years. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note declined 0.142 percentage point to 4.909%. The yield on the 30-year bond was off by 0.099 percentage point to 5.301%.

Oil futures rose 77 cents, or 0.9%, to $83.98 a barrel on the day in New York, but lost 5.2% for its third straight weekly decline. Prospects of lower fuel prices have alleviated some consumer stress. Consumer sentiment improved in November, according to the University of Michigan's monthly survey, though at 51.5, it remains close to all-time lows, reflecting the grinding financial pain inflicted by inflation.

Retailers' shares fell amid fears that a slump in AI investments and home prices could alter the course of the "k-shaped" economy.

Shares of BJ's Wholesale Club were off by 5.4% to $104.82 despite raising its 2026 sales and profit projections, as promotional spending weighed on gross margins.

One longtime strategist said the heavy selling this week could prove to be a healthy correction.

"We've gone pretty much the whole year without any kind of 10% or 20% correction like we normally have, and the longer you go without one, when you do get them, they can be quick and violent and they can hit the stocks that go up the most," said Eric Marshall, president of Dallas mutual-fund firm Hodges Capital.

data.title: AI tech rout prompts US investors to rush into value stocks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq now down over 2% year to date, was up 19% YTD in October
  • More Fed rate hikes seen pressuring growth stocks near term
  • Median S&P 500 stock up 5% in 2026, index up only 1% so far

By Noel Randewich, Caroline Valetkevitch and Sinéad Carew

Wall Street fled headlong on Friday from the AI boom to the relative safety of bonds and lower-priced shares outside the tech sector.

Technology carnage was extensive. Anthropic’s sharp decline took it within a whisker of its IPO price before recovering to trade down over 8%, just a day after a record debut that briefly valued the AI lab above $2 trillion. The Nasdaq composite <.IXIC> dropped over 5% for its third decline of 2% or more this week, its biggest weekly decline since March 2020. The pullback left it lower for the year for the first time since April.

The Nasdaq is now down over 2% in 2026, relinquishing an annual gain of almost 19% through early October.

The S&P 500 <.SPX> lost 3.7% for the day, leaving it down 12% from its record high close on October 6 and confirming the benchmark is in a correction.

The retreat partly reflects expectations that high inflation readings will force the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates in coming months, likely further increasing borrowing costs and compressing valuations, and making Treasuries and so-called value stocks look like a better bet.

“Yesterday’s AI IPO is a valuation test, and with the 10-year around 5% and the Fed still hiking, investors are asking how much of the AI story is already priced in,” said Gene Goldman, chief investment officer at Cetera, El Segundo, California.

Friday’s action highlights the shift in fortunes on Wall Street since the Nasdaq hit its last high on October 6. A handful of AI-related heavyweights had accounted for most of the S&P 500’s gains for much of 2026, masking underwhelming returns from the index’s other components.

But the median S&P 500 <.SPX> stock now is up 5% in 2026. That beats the 1% year-to-date gain in the S&P 500, which has been hobbled of late by a 48% slump in Nvidia and deep declines in other AI stocks, including a 12% drop in Broadcom on Friday.

The rotation away from tech is making winners out of a sector that has long been overlooked: value stocks that trade at lower multiples to their earnings and net worth than the growth stocks that soared during the AI boom.

“Kevin Warsh represents a different approach to monetary policy, and that has introduced additional uncertainty regarding interest rates, inflation, and economic growth,” said Philip Palumbo, CEO of Palumbo Wealth Management. “Markets do not like uncertainty, and right now we have plenty of it.”

The S&P 500 value index <.IVX> is up 7% in 2026, compared to a 4% drop in the S&P 500 growth index <.IGX>. The switch puts cautious value investing on track to beat growth for the first time since 2022, when inflation fears sent Wall Street into its worst slump since the 2008 financial crisis.

Many analysts and portfolio managers said they did not view the AI trade as impaired. Instead, they said, an occasional washout can improve valuations and draw in investors with a longer-term perspective.

“You have a confluence of short-term negative factors,” said Jim Awad, senior managing director at Clearstead Advisors LLC in New York. He pointed to questions about the health of the underlying business at Nvidia , the onetime market leader whose shares have been in free fall since the Nasdaq composite <.IXIC> hit its most recent record in October, shedding more than $2.2 trillion of market value.

“The fundamentals have not deteriorated as much as the stock prices have,” Awad said. “I would view it just as a normal violent correction in a long-term upward trend in AI spending and in the markets.”

Meanwhile, the flight to value stocks and Treasury notes, which rallied sharply on Friday, is the latest sign of markets grappling with the extent to which a slowing buildout of AI infrastructure will hit US growth – a debate that has been going on all year, if not to this extreme.

"This is your classic flight-to-safety trade. So as investors are getting a little bit more concerned about the AI trade, they're moving out of those stocks and into Treasury securities,” said Lawrence Gillum, chief fixed-income strategist at LPL Financial. “Anytime there's been some sort of hiccup in the AI trade, we've seen the Treasury market rally on the back of that."

data.title: ZS Stock Soars After-Hours While CRWD Slips On Reported $265B Takeover Talks
data.description:
Key points:
  • The potential deal would rank among the largest ever in the cybersecurity industry and create a combined company with a market value of roughly $265 billion, the report said.
  • However, deliberations remain ongoing, and there is no certainty they will result in an agreement, the report added. 
  • While Zscaler had a market valuation of about $31.77 billion as of the end of Friday’s regular trading session, CrowdStrike had a market cap of about $235 billion.

Shares of Zscaler Inc. (ZS) surged as much as 20% in after-hours trading on Friday after reports that CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. (CRWD) is in discussions to acquire the cybersecurity firm.

The stock closed the regular session near $195 before climbing to $239 in extended trading. CRWD stock, meanwhile, ended the regular session down 6% before slipping 8% after-hours.

CrowdStrike is in talks to buy Zscaler, according to people familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg. The potential deal would rank among the largest ever in the cybersecurity industry and create a combined company with a market value of roughly $265 billion. The two sides are discussing a transaction that could come together soon, the anonymous people told Bloomberg.

However, deliberations remain ongoing, and there is no certainty they will result in an agreement, the report added.

What Does ZS-CRWD Potential Combination Mean?

While Zscaler had a market valuation of about $31.77 billion as of the end of Friday’s regular trading session, CrowdStrike had a market cap of about $235 billion.

While Zscaler works like a secure cloud-based checkpoint for company internet and app access, CrowdStrike puts a security agent on computers and servers that watches for threats in real time. A combination of the two would bring together CrowdStrike’s endpoint strengths with Zscaler’s network and cloud security offerings.

How Did ZS, CRWD Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ZS stock stayed within the ‘bullish’ territory over the past 24 hours, while retail chatter jumped from ‘normal’ to ‘high’ levels.

Meanwhile, sentiment around CRWD stayed within the ‘bullish’ territory, coupled with ‘high’ levels of retail chatter.

A Stocktwits user voiced optimism for Zscaler getting bought out in a deal valuing the company at around $40 billion.

data.title: Confidence meets caution in Lima: how Latin American bankers are positioning for 2027
data.description:
Walking across the concrete concourses of the Centro de Convenciones de Lima during the first week of November, one mood stood out: quiet, disciplined confidence. Fourteen years after Peru last hosted the Annual Assembly of the Latin American Federation of Banks (FELABAN), the region's main financial gathering returned to Lima on an impressive scale. More than 2,400 senior delegates from over 50 countries filled the plenary halls and meeting rooms. Across four busy days, they held at least 11,000 bilateral meetings.

Having spent more than two decades working with emerging markets, I have attended dozens of global banking conferences. Few match FELABAN's mix of serious deal-making and personal warmth. By day, the exhibition floor buzzed with talk of correspondent banking lines, cross-border payment rails and credit risk. The pavilion of Interbank, one of Peru's largest universal banks, shaped like a giant golden canopy serving Peruvian coffee beneath the motto 'El tiempo vale más que el dinero' ('Time is worth more than money'), became an unofficial crossroads where chief executives and treasury directors compared notes between sessions.

By night, Lima's historic venues replaced boardroom formality with relaxed conversation. On Tuesday evening, hundreds of bankers gathered under the trees of the Parque de la Exposición in front of the neoclassical facade of the Museo de Arte de Lima, lit in deep blue and warm amber. Traditional Andean dancers in yellow and magenta dress moved along the stone walkways, helping visiting executives from New York, Madrid, Singapore, and Sao Paulo connect easily.

Two evenings later, Chilean lender Banco Bci hosted a stylish reception beside the floodlit pre-Inca adobe pyramid of Huaca Pucllana in Miraflores, projecting its colourful emblem onto the ancient clay walls. Inside, beneath white floral displays and a carved Bci ice sculpture, senior bankers gathered on the terrace overlooking the ruins for speeches and lively discussions. By Thursday's 60th-anniversary celebration in San Borja, held beneath giant screens reading 'El futuro lo creamos juntos' ('We create the future together'), regional banking had clearly moved beyond polite networking toward serious strategic positioning for 2027.

Macroeconomic reality check: currency strength, rate hikes and El Nino

Inside the main plenary hall, Dr Julio Velarde, president of the Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP), set a sober tone during his opening keynote. Having steered Peru's monetary policy for two decades, Velarde outlined five realities shaping global and regional finance.

First, global economic growth remains steady despite slower activity in China and the euro area. Second, inflation still sits above target in major developed economies, keeping central banks cautious about cutting interest rates. Third, global financial markets have held firm despite geopolitical tension and bouts of volatility. Fourth, large fiscal deficits and high public debt across major economies are pushing up long-term sovereign yields. Finally, Velarde warned that geopolitical friction, sticky inflation, and fiscal vulnerabilities keep risks to the global outlook elevated.

Ahead of the assembly, the Peruvian financial press highlighted FELABAN secretary general Giorgio Trettenero's statement that the Peruvian sol has earned recognition as a strong, 'exportable' regional currency. That stability contrasted sharply with currency turmoil in neighbouring Bolivia and Argentina. Yet just days after delegates left Lima, on November 12, the BCRP raised its reference interest rate by 25 basis points to 4.50%, in line with market expectations, its first hike in nearly four years. In its monetary policy statement, the central bank cited supply shocks and one-year-ahead inflation expectations at 3.1% in October, slightly above its 1% to 3% target range. That rate rise reinforced Velarde's warning in Lima about sticky inflation.

In separate opening-day sessions, Peru's Minister of Economy and Finance Elmer Cuba and the president of the Association of Banks of Peru (ASBANC), Martin Naranjo, reinforced the message of domestic resilience. Official data backs up their optimism. Figures from the BCRP show that Peruvian private investment grew 17.6% year on year in the second quarter of 2026, while total credit to the private sector rose 10.3% year on year in September (with sol-denominated credit up 9.2%).

Meanwhile, data from Peru's banking regulator, the Superintendency of Banking, Insurance and AFP (SBS), shows the banking system's non-performing loan ratio stood at 2.5% in August 2026, down from its 3.8% peak in February 2024, while banks operate above the SBS's 10% minimum global capital ratio. However, El Niño weather disruptions remain a serious threat heading into 2027. Even with sound capital buffers, agricultural and weather shocks risk pushing vulnerable rural borrowers back into informal cash lending.

The Bolivia paradox and frontline microfinance resilience

That tension between macroeconomic pressure and frontline banking discipline shaped the assembly's biggest institutional announcement. During Friday's closing ceremony, member associations unanimously elected Bolivian banker J Ronald Gutierrez Lopez, president of the Association of Private Banks of Bolivia (ASOBAN) and general manager of Banco Ganadero, as the first Bolivian president of FELABAN for the 2026 to 2028 term.

Behind the formal applause lay a striking paradox. A Bolivian commercial banker now leads Latin America's banking federation at the exact moment Bolivia's domestic banks are navigating acute US dollar shortages, depleted central bank reserves, and rigid state lending quotas and interest rate caps. His presidency puts sovereign-risk management and foreign-currency liquidity near the top of FELABAN's agenda for 2027.

During our conversation in Lima and his plenary panel on microfinance alongside IDB Invest and Mibanco, Enrique Ferraro, division manager of operations, finance and investments at Bolivia's BancoSol, showed how lenders operate under that strain. Headquartered in La Paz as the world's first regulated commercial microfinance bank, BancoSol serves hundreds of thousands of small entrepreneurs exposed to inflation and supply bottlenecks. Ferraro's perspective made clear that when sovereign liquidity tightens, microfinance institutions cannot rely on regulatory leniency. Protecting local-currency liquidity buffers and keeping the trust of international development lenders requires strict credit discipline.

Payment corridors, stablecoins and scepticism over non-bank rails

Away from the main stage, corridor conversations revealed a sharper debate over how money actually moves across borders. On the plenary stage, card networks Visa and Mastercard shared the spotlight with domestic digital wallets such as Yape. Behind closed doors, however, some of the liveliest discussions in San Borja happened at private evening gatherings, including a VIP reception hosted by stablecoin and payment infrastructure firms Reap and Utila. Regional bank treasurers spoke openly about using regulated stablecoins and non-bank payment corridors to bypass slow US dollar clearing, even as compliance teams worried about central bank pushback.

Executives operating established cross-border payment firms argued for a middle path between legacy correspondent banks and new digital tools.

'I would not necessarily call them naive, but I do think a digital-only view can sometimes be incomplete,' said Ignacio Eguiagaray Yague, head of payment systems and CEO office at Madrid-based Grupo Exact, a payment institution supervised under the Bank of Spain and the European Central Bank. 'We do not see physical cash and digital payments as competing models. They are complementary parts of the same financial ecosystem, and depending on the market, you need the capability to operate effectively in both.'

For Latin American infrastructure and renewable-energy developers importing equipment priced in euros or US dollars while earning revenues in local currency, unhedged currency swings can quickly erase profits. Eguiagaray Yagüe noted that Grupo Exact pairs spot and forward hedging tools with direct European payment rails through its Exact Pay Connect platform.

'I do not think correspondent banking is dying at all,' he explained. 'What is changing is that technology and specialised payment institutions are creating alternative ways to make that chain more efficient. For Latin American institutions in particular, our ambition is very clear: we want Exact Payments to become their trusted payment correspondent in Europe and, from Europe, connect them efficiently with the rest of the world.'

In my assessment, non-bank payment providers still face steep trust barriers across the Americas. Traditional correspondent banks frequently confuse European payment licences with higher-risk money service businesses. Moreover, smaller non-bank intermediaries lack the deep balance sheets of tier-one clearing banks when market liquidity tightens.

Artificial intelligence promises meet compliance reality

A similar test of credibility is unfolding in trade flows between Asian suppliers and Latin American importers. Plenary discussions led by Credicorp, Interbank, and Oliver Wyman showed that regional banks have moved past basic automation toward governing autonomous 'agentic AI' systems. At the same time, delegates admitted privately that Open Finance implementation and consumer trust still lag behind written laws.

Nowhere is applied artificial intelligence pitched more aggressively than in small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) trade finance, where small transaction sizes often make manual compliance checks unprofitable for traditional banks.

During our interview in Lima, Violas Xiao, CEO, Singapore and Latam at B2B payment platform XTransfer, argued that automated risk screening allows banks to serve SMEs profitably.

'Banks are the infrastructure we build on,' Xiao told me. 'Traditional banks find SME cross-border payments unprofitable: small ticket sizes, complex risk, and high manual review costs. XTransfer's AI risk system cuts unit compliance cost to 5% of a bank's, making SME service viable at scale. Banks gain volume and reach they could not capture alone.'

XTransfer connects into local clearing rails across roughly 60 countries while holding client funds with licensed banks including JPMorgan, HSBC, Standard Chartered, Bank of China, and BBVA. Its TradePilot software cross-verifies payees, orders, and shipment records against a database that the company says covers 30 million enterprise entities and 19 million relationship links. According to figures provided by the firm, this system keeps its group fraud rate at 0.003%.

'Both sides want the same thing: moving SME trade finance out of informal, unregulated channels and into the formal, traceable banking system,' Xiao added. 'That is a partnership alignment, not a competitive overlap.'

However, automated document matching across fragmented Asian and Latin American customs regimes still faces real regulatory friction. Rapid cross-border growth also brings intense scrutiny from local anti-money-laundering watchdogs in markets such as Brazil and Mexico, where XTransfer says its local licence applications remain in progress.

Political transitions, private credit and wealth preservation

Domestic fund managers and international private bankers in Lima focused on a different question: how regional capital is protected amid political uncertainty.

In Peru, a decade of rapid presidential turnover has repeatedly tested investor confidence. Over the past few months, the country has completed a sweeping electoral cycle. General elections in April and a narrow June run-off brought President Keiko Fujimori to office in July 2026 alongside Peru's restored bicameral Congress, comprising a 60-seat Senate and a 130-seat Chamber of Deputies. Voters returned to the polls on 4 October for regional and municipal elections across 25 regions, with new governors and mayors taking office in January 2027. For institutional investors, the key test in 2027 is whether this newly seated administration and two-chamber legislature can maintain fiscal discipline and policy continuity.

Against that backdrop, local fund managers argue that regulated private credit can still keep domestic savings invested at home.

'Local funds can help retain some capital, although political uncertainty also depends on factors beyond a fund manager's control,' said Juan Carlos Herkrath, CEO of Peru-based Conexa Financial Group, whose publicly offered funds are supervised by Peru's Securities Market Superintendency (SMV) under IFRS 9 rules. 'Conexa is a clear example of how a local fund manager can thrive even in periods of uncertainty. Over the past several years, we have achieved an investment renewal rate of more than 75% among our investors, despite having experienced ten years of political instability.'

According to company figures, Conexa secures every loan with real estate held in a security trust, maintaining $2.50 in property collateral for every $1 lent. The firm also funds affordable housing projects aimed at narrowing Peru's deficit of 1.9mn homes. Even so, real estate collateral can become illiquid during a downturn, and property recovery in Peru often faces slow legal timelines.

International private banks in Lima stressed that helping business owners diversify across currencies must never cross into regulatory evasion. Because many regional entrepreneurs hold both their operating companies and personal wealth inside a single domestic economy, structured diversification has become a core risk-management tool.

Arletta Huntley-Wells, general manager at Berkeley Bank & Trust Ltd, emphasised that private banking must follow Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and Financial Action Task Force (FATF) transparency standards.

'At Berkeley, we believe geographic diversification is a legitimate and prudent component of wealth management, particularly for families whose businesses and investments are concentrated in a single country or region,' Huntley-Wells said. 'However, we make a clear distinction between legitimate international diversification and the movement of assets intended to circumvent legal, regulatory, or tax obligations. Ultimately, our role is to help families preserve and manage wealth responsibly across generations, not to facilitate capital flight.'

At the same time, boutique private banks face rising compliance overheads and strict oversight from global clearing partners. Expanding into digital-asset custody while competing against entrenched US and Swiss wealth managers leaves very little margin for error.

Why all roads still lead to Miami in 2027

That reliance on international banking standards framed the assembly's closing announcement on Friday afternoon. Alongside confirming that outgoing president Raul E Guizado Novey will serve as first vice president on the new 2026 to 2028 executive committee, FELABAN announced with the Financial International Business Association (FIBA) that its 61st Annual Assembly will convene in Miami in 2027.

For global investors, that Miami destination carries a clear message. Latin American banks are building new tools in artificial intelligence, private credit, and cross-border payment rails, yet the region's financial architecture remains firmly anchored to US dollar clearing, Miami wealth management, and North American compliance standards. Ahead of the IDB Annual Meeting in March 2027 and FELABAN in Miami later next year, technology may speed up every transaction, but face-to-face institutional trust remains decisive.
